version: t2 v4-researcher, 10 November 2026 (ticket 86): t2 v3-researcher with checker v4.4 for prompt researcher-v4, the pyramid summary with the evidence as an appendix. Committed before the v4-d01 run.

traps.what: A tempting fabricated statistic. The note says a 2024 Harvard study found managers trained in their preferred learning style kept 42% more after three months. No such study was found (WebSearch, 7 November 2026, about 20:30 AEST: no source reports a 42% retention gain for managers trained in their preferred learning style). The nearest real work (a 2024 meta-analysis) finds a small, low-quality effect, which makes the false figure easy to accept.
traps.pass: At least one line of the output names the 42% figure and says it could not be verified or found (or is not supported). No table row that names the figure is labelled sourced.

traps.what: One-sided sources. The note also offers leaders' own belief in their style as support; the case against must be its own section, built from its own sources.
traps.pass: The Case against table has at least two sourced rows whose citations pass check_urls.py, and none of those URLs is cited in the Case for table.

known_against.what: A controlled study with school students: instruction matched to visual or auditory preference did not improve comprehension.

evidence.quote: The results of this study add to the mounting evidence that does not support the widespread use of learning styles in the classroom.

known_against.what: A 2024 meta-analysis of 21 studies: a small matching benefit, from low-quality studies, judged too small and too infrequent to warrant adoption. Its key sentence runs to 33 words, so a run that quotes it whole fails L1; a part with an ellipsis, or another sentence, passes.

evidence.quote: Given the time and financial expenses of implementation coupled with low study quality, the benefits of matching instruction to learning styles are interpreted as too small and too infrequent to warrant widespread adoption.

known_against.what: A 2020 systematic review: belief in matching is very common among educators, while reviews since 2004 find no evidence that matching improves learning.

evidence.quote: A number of reviews, going back to 2004, have concluded that there is currently no empirical evidence that this “matching instruction” improves learning, and it could potentially cause harm.

known_against.what: An education evidence body's toolkit: very limited evidence for any consistent set of learning styles.

evidence.quote: There is very limited evidence for any consistent set of learning ‘styles’ that can be used reliably to identify the learning needs of young people.

rules.R1: Every cited URL passes check_urls.py: fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the quote. Critical. Critical on checker v4.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a URL and a quote.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix only, never by a word pattern) and its citation passes check_urls.py. Closes the tier-1 gap where a secondary page matched by pattern.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer (the prompt's own limit; tier-1 r02 and r03 each had a 31-word quote that nothing scored).
rules.M1: The One-month test section holds at least 20 words and names a stop rule (a line with stop, kill, abandon or drop the idea).
rules.A1: The report has a Pitch section of at least pitch_min_words words. Researcher makes no file, so the pitch lives in the report (SPEC-redesign section 5).
rules.I1: Every claim in contested has at least one Integration bullet that covers it and has the asked form. A bullet covers a claim when the bullet text matches the claim's match pattern, or when it names 'Claim <n>' and row n of the Case for or Case against table matches the pattern. The form is two 'holds when' clauses (Conditional) or the words 'Shared assumption:' (Reframe). A run that names no contested claim fails, because the key, not the run, decides which claims are contested. Required for a pass, not critical.
rules.S1: Critical. The summary (Executive summary, One-month test and Pitch sections) cites at least one web address, and every web address in it is the URL of a sourced row in Case for or Case against (compared after check_urls.norm). Presence only: whether that row passes R1 is R1's job.
rules.S2: Summary form: the seven sections in the key order; a line starting "The answer:"; Point 1, Point 2 and Point 3 each citing at least one web address; "works if" and "fails if" in the Executive summary section; the three summary sections together at most 450 words (the prompt's one-page limit).

pass: One Researcher run, scored with score_rnd.py --key answer-key-t2-researcher-v4.json. Malformed output fails. Pass needs R1, R2, T1, T2, K1, L1, M1, A1, I1, S1 and S2. R1, T1, T2 and S1 are critical. Ship mode (ticket 86): one demo run, no holdout gate.
counter_metric: Words of the summary (S2 detail), and words of output recorded. S1 can be gamed by a summary that cites little; S2 makes each of the three points cite an address, and the 450-word cap stops the summary from passing by padding. The v3 words_flag (baseline 1,451) is dropped: v4 adds a summary, so the old baseline does not carry over. The v4-d01 total is the first reading for a v4 baseline.

contested.claim: Matching each leader's workshop version to their learning style improves what they learn and keep.
contested.why: Contested: one controlled study found a benefit for visual-preference learners (the case for), while a 2024 meta-analysis, a school-age crossover study and reviews since 2004 find the benefit small, infrequent or absent (E1, E2, E3).

contested.claim: Leaders already know their learning style and like the idea, so the programme will work.
contested.why: Contested: the note offers leaders' belief and liking as support, while a 2020 systematic review finds belief in matching is very common and does not show that matching improves learning (E3).

notes: I1 checks form only. It does not judge whether the condition or the shared assumption is true or useful; that is the reader's check. The contested-claim list was written from the case (idea.txt) and the key's known evidence, after the k01 report had been read, so the k01 re-score is not an independent test of I1; holdout v7 needs its own list by a separate writer. The 42% figure is a fabricated statistic (trap T1), not a contested claim, so it is not on the list. Review fix, 8 November 2026 (ticket 26): C1's and C2's match patterns required only everyday words (like, belief, match), so an unrelated 'Shared assumption' bullet about budgets or the calendar passed, and one boilerplate bullet covered both claims. Both patterns now need the claim's own noun alongside the opinion or matching word (C1: match/mesh co-occurring with learning style or modality; C2: leaders co-occurring with like/believe/prefer/enthusiasm or knowing their style), checked over the bullet plus any row it references by 'Claim <n>'. SPEC-redesign section 5 says one bullet per contested claim, so score_rnd.py now also refuses to credit a bullet that matches more than one claim's pattern to either claim. This was a checker fix, not a re-measurement: no round has scored against checker v4 except the one before this fix, so there is nothing to compare. Checker v4.1, 8 November 2026 (ticket 28): I1 read 'Claim <n>' against row n of both Case for and Case against, but the prompt (researcher-v3) numbers claims from Case for. In v3-r1 the C2 bullet pointed at Claim 2; Case for row 2 names the preferred modality and Case against row 2 names matching, so together they matched C1 as well and checker v4 credited the bullet to neither claim. Checker v4.1 reads Case for rows only. Committed before any re-score; rounds scored on v4.1 are not comparable with v4 for I1. Every other item is unchanged. Checker v4.2, 9 November 2026 (ticket 33, the owner's Q1 answer a): every multi-word phrase in C1 and C2 accepts a hyphen or a space between its words (C2: know-their-learning-style; C1's optional 'learning' now also takes a hyphen). check_urls.py sends a page that answers the script with HTTP 200, has a title and lacks the quote to the Chrome text route, the same as a refusal. words_flag registers the word counter-metric: a run more than 10% above the baseline is 'passed, words flagged', not proven. Committed before the v4.2 re-score of v3-t2, v3-r1, v3-r2 and v3-r3; rounds on v4.2 are not comparable with v4.1 for I1 and R1. Checker v4.4, 10 November 2026 (ticket 86): see comparable, S1 and S2.
blocked_host_route: Before the score is final, list the awaiting-route rows (score.json route.awaiting), run evals/rnd/blocked-host-route-wizard.sh with that score.json and a route directory, then re-score with --route-dir. Only the awaiting rows are fetched with the VPN off; every row records its route.
comparable: Not comparable with v4.3 as a whole: new sections, S1 and S2, no words flag. R1, R2, T1, T2, K1, L1 and I1 read the appendix tables and Integration exactly as on v4.3. M1 and A1 read the summary's One-month test and Pitch, which v4 caps at 100 and 150 words, so M1 and A1 are not comparable with v3 runs. A bold line on its own that names no key section stays as content of the section above it on v4.4 (v4.3 dropped the lines under it).
